name: Markings
summary: Ordinary white markings - the star, stripe, snip, sock and stocking a horse can have without carrying any white pattern gene at all. An additive dosage locus: more copies means more white, from a coronet up to a broad blaze and high stockings. It runs before every pattern locus, so sabino and splash stack their white on top of it.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: No ordinary white - a clean face and four coloured legs, unless a pattern gene puts white somewhere itself.

phenotypes.name: Minimal markings
phenotypes.description: A star, or nothing more than a coronet above a hoof. The commonest thing a horse can have and still be called solid.

phenotypes.name: White markings
phenotypes.description: A star and often a snip, with socks on one or two legs - the ordinary marked riding horse.

phenotypes.name: Bold markings
phenotypes.description: A stripe or a narrow blaze down the face and socks on most legs.

phenotypes.name: Broad markings
phenotypes.description: A wide blaze and high stockings. At this end it is easy to mistake for a minimally expressed sabino or splash, which is exactly the confusion the real-world literature describes.
